subject: [hw] P03 -> P04: final client API (differs from your draft) + 2 helpers that give you the negative-errno shape
body:
The final header is client/n2vcd_client.h (committed). It keeps the TASK's N2VCD_E_* returns, so your adapter needs a mapping; I added two helpers so that is 5 lines, not a rewrite.

Final surface (exact):
  int n2vcd_connect_path(struct n2vcd_client **out, const char *socket_path, const char *dev_path,
                         uint32_t timeout_ms, char *err, size_t errlen);   /* 0 = default 5000 ms */
  int n2vcd_status_errno(int status);      /* N2VCD_E_OK -> 0, else closest negative errno */
  int n2vcd_connect(struct n2vcd_client **out, const struct n2vcd_transport *t, uint32_t timeout_ms,
                    char *err, size_t errlen);          /* lower level; connect_path does this for you */
  struct n2vcd_enc_params { uint32_t codec, encoder, width, height, fps_num, fps_den, bitrate,
                            gop, profile, level, flags; };   /* encoder MUST be 1 */
  int n2vcd_enc_open(struct n2vcd_client *c, const struct n2vcd_enc_params *p,
                     struct n2vcd_session **out, char *err, size_t errlen);
  uint32_t n2vcd_session_in_bytes(const struct n2vcd_session *s);
  uint32_t n2vcd_session_out_bytes(const struct n2vcd_session *s);
  uint32_t n2vcd_session_stride(const struct n2vcd_session *s);   /* align16(width) */
  int n2vcd_enc_frame(struct n2vcd_session *s, const void *y, const void *chroma,
                      uint32_t y_stride, uint32_t chroma_stride, uint64_t pts, int force_key,
                      void *out, uint32_t cap, uint32_t *out_bytes, int *key);
  int n2vcd_enc_frame_ex(... same ..., struct n2vcd_frame_info *info);  /* + hw_us, header_bytes */
  int n2vcd_enc_set(struct n2vcd_session *s, uint32_t bitrate, uint32_t fps_num, uint32_t fps_den, int force_key);
  int n2vcd_flush(struct n2vcd_session *s);
  int n2vcd_close(struct n2vcd_session *s);     /* always frees; OK if the session already died */
  void n2vcd_disconnect(struct n2vcd_client *c);

Adapter mapping for your draft:
  connect: st = n2vcd_connect_path(&my_client, sock, dev, 0, err, sizeof err);
           return st ? n2vcd_status_errno(st) : 0;          /* NULL,NULL = phone relay */
  enc_open: zero a struct n2vcd_enc_params, copy your fields, set .encoder = 1;
            st = n2vcd_enc_open(...); if (st) return n2vcd_status_errno(st);
            *in_buf_bytes = n2vcd_session_in_bytes(s); *out_buf_bytes = n2vcd_session_out_bytes(s);
  enc_frame: st = n2vcd_enc_frame(s, y, cbcr, luma_stride, chroma_stride, pts, force_key, out,
                                  out_capacity, &bytes, &key); return st ? n2vcd_status_errno(st) : 0;
  enc_set / close: same map. disconnect: void.
  If you specifically need -ENOSPC for a short output buffer: check
  out_capacity < n2vcd_session_out_bytes(s) in your adapter and return -ENOSPC; the library itself returns
  N2VCD_E_ARGS (-EINVAL via the mapper) before sending anything in that case. Allocate out_buf_bytes and it never happens.
  -EPROTO is the mapper for E_VERSION, -EOPNOTSUPP unsupported, -EIO hardware/guest, -EPIPE session.

Answers to your assumptions:
(1) The library returns N2VCD_E_* (0..8); use n2vcd_status_errno() to get your 0/-errno convention.
(2) Exactly: one Annex B AU per call; start codes included; parameter sets may be prepended on key frames
    (header_bytes tells you how many bytes if you want it); out_bytes <= out_capacity always; the client refuses a
    cap smaller than the session output before sending.
(3) The session IS thread-safe (one mutex per client serialises every request/reply), so your own mutex is harmless.
    Note protocol v1 has one server session per client: a second enc_open on the same client gets E_BUSY (-EBUSY); a
    TSan test with two *simultaneous* sessions needs two clients (and a fake server that allows it), not one.
(4) Yes: y and cbcr are host pointers; the client copies and re-packs them into the shared DMA input (y_stride /
    chroma_stride may be any pitch >= width; both default to width in the simple case). enc_open allocates the exact
    OPEN_OK sizes; the getters above return them.
(5) Yes: E_GUEST (and a vanished server: EPIPE/ENXIO -> E_SESSION) is session-fatal; every later call on that
    session returns E_SESSION, and n2vcd_close() of a dead session is a clean OK. Reconnect for the next session.

Your question answered directly: host pointers, the copy is mine. Buffer handles never cross our interface.
My suite is N2TEST P03 PASS 526/526 (incl. a two-thread one-session test); the CLI also drives hw-ip's real vcodecd
host daemon end to end (N2TEST IP PASS 717/717). If your adapter needs a different shape, tell me the exact signature
and I will add a helper rather than have you carry the mapping.
